title: A faster, lighter C# Dev Kit
author: Drew Noakes
note: Version 11.0 rebuilds the extension as one Native AOT process with cached project loading. In Microsoft's benchmark on the 407-project Aspire repo, full solution load drops from 84 s to 3 s and memory from about 2 GB to 316 MB; it's in pre-release for now.

title: Aspire 13.6: Your dashboard gets memory
author: Maddy Montaquila
note: The dashboard now keeps traces, logs and resource state after you stop the AppHost (up to 10 runs, stored locally in SQLite). You can go back to the run where a bug showed up, and the new opt-in WithRepl() opens a signed-in database shell right in the dashboard.

title: Microsoft is updating its NuGet author-signing certificate
author: NuGet Team
note: If you enforce trusted signers or run dotnet nuget verify with Microsoft fingerprints, installs fail with NU3034 until you add the new certificate fingerprint.

title: AG-UI Protocol now has a first-class .NET SDK
author: Daniel Roth
note: Microsoft and CopilotKit released an MIT-licensed .NET SDK for AG-UI, the open protocol for streaming agent events to user-facing apps. Any .NET service can now expose or consume agent endpoints that work with TypeScript and Python clients.

title: Build Agentic UI with the new Blazor AI components
author: Daniel Roth
note: The experimental Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI package renders streamed agent output, tool calls, approval prompts and shared state as Blazor components, on top of any IChatClient. Try it with the .NET 11 RC1 SDK and the AgenticUI sample.

title: Visual Studio September Update
author: Mark Downie
note: Bring Your Own Model (preview) now runs on the new Agent (Preview), with Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama. The old BYOM flow is gone and Ollama models need re-adding.

title: UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest
author: Amaury Levé
note: MSTest 4.5 can run UWP and WinUI 3 tests on the app's real UI dispatcher, across packaged, unpackaged and AppContainer hosts. Packaged hosts need Developer Mode, so check your CI agent first.

title: Experimental support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in ASP.NET Core
author: Andrew Lock
note: .NET 11 adds experimental DBSC support to ASP.NET Core with one call, AddDeviceBoundSession(...). It ties a login session to a key in the device's TPM, so a stolen auth cookie stops working quickly.

title: File-based apps can reference other C# files
author: Denis Makarenko
note: The new #:ref directive lets a dotnet run app.cs program pull in a second C# file. On .NET 11 RC1 it's still behind an experimental property.

title: What's Inside That Bearer Token? A Practical Guide to Encrypted JWTs (JWE) in .NET
author: Robert Dennyson
note: A walkthrough of spotting, inspecting and decrypting encrypted JWTs with JsonWebTokenHandler. Decryption and validation are separate steps, and any token pasted into a chat or log should be treated as exposed.

title: How to Make AI Write High-Quality Code in .NET
author: Anton Martyniuk
note: Rules written in prompts fade as an agent's context fills up, so the article moves them into the build with TreatWarningsAsErrors, analyzers, .editorconfig and Central Package Management.

title: Stripping extra dependencies in .NET NativeAOT apps using linker substitutions
author: Andrew Lock
note: An ILLink.Substitutions.xml file turns a runtime check into a constant, so the linker can remove code it couldn't prove was unused. In Andrew's case that cut a NativeAOT binary by 22 to 25 percent.
